name: winged zebrafish, flying-fish fins - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion set to the flying fish's MEASURED median

A_DIFFERENT_DESIGN_FROM.difference: winged-zebrafish sets pectoral_len_over_SL = 0.35, a CHOSEN point between the zebrafish placeholder (0.155) and the flying-fish median (0.687). This design sets it to 0.687 itself.
A_DIFFERENT_DESIGN_FROM.why_it_matters: 0.35 was picked; 0.687 is measured. This design therefore rests on the one evidence-backed proportion available in the whole project, which is a better basis than the chosen value - but only for THIS parameter. Everything else about the animal is still generated, and the animal itself is still a design, not a described species.

real_experimental_counterpart.what: No real fish has a zebrafish body with flying-fish pectoral proportions. The nearest real experiment, the germline lat4a nr21/+ ; kcnh2a lof/+ double heterozygote (genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B), has 'overgrown' paired fins reported only in figure panels, with no numeric pectoral length in text, legends or Data S1. Nothing is digitised here, and that fish is NOT this design.
real_experimental_counterpart.caveat: Transferring a flying-fish fin proportion onto a zebrafish body is an assumption about shape, not a demonstrated developmental possibility.

pectoral_len_over_SL.reason: set to the flying fish's measured median pectoral length / SL, so that the design's lifting surface rests on a measurement rather than on a chosen intermediate value. Motivated by a glide requirement: at 0.35 the 1:1 print's minimum glide speed is far above anything the animal could reach.

pectoral_span_over_SL.reason: span follows the fin length, the same convention the winged-zebrafish design uses, so span and area scale together and the fish's own aspect-ratio convention is preserved

pectoral_area_over_SL2.reason: area follows length^1.834 (Davenport 1992 exponent, development/trajectory.mjs P.area.exp); an assumed transfer from flying fish to zebrafish, identical in form to the winged-zebrafish design's delta and differing only in the length ratio it is raised from

evidence_note: Daane 2021 Data S1A reports the flying-fish pectoral length / SL median as 0.687 over n = 49. That number is measured. Its application to a zebrafish body is not: no fish with this combination has been observed, and nothing here shows such a fin could develop on this body.
caveat_morphological_not_genetic: MORPHOLOGICAL interpolation, not genetic hybridisation. Averaging or transplanting two species' body parameters says nothing about whether such an animal could be bred, is viable, or is developmentally reachable; genomes do not average. Flying fish and zebrafish are not crossable. This is a shape, not an organism.
